newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes firmer as revival continues.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes firmer as revival continues.

text.p: Gold prices crept higher in aftrnoon trading on Thursday after an attempt to sell the market lower earlier was beaten off, dealers said.
But opinion remained divided on whether or not the selling was on behalf of a central bank.
"There were rumours that a European central bank was selling, especially during the Tokyo time frame," a dealer said.

But another dismissed the idea of central bank selling coming in overnight. "That selling was not like a central bank which tries not to disrupt the market. This morning was a deliberate attempt to push the price down," he said.
Gold fixed slightly firmer from the morning at $369.00 per ounce up 70 cents and compared with $370.90 on Wednesday.
The Comex February contract was down about $1.70 at $370.80 shortly after the fixing.

"We are seeing some fresh buying and some of the funds have begun to cover some shorts," one dealer said, adding that the Wednesday high of around $371 could be reached if further covering took place.
Gold looked to have established good support at between $366 and $367, the dealer added.
Another dealer said that London had probably gone net short of gold given the amount sold earlier.
The market was still essentially bearish, dealers said.
The fall in U.S. share values late on Tuesday coupled with weakness in the dollar helped lift gold off a three-year low reached as the market became oversold and in need of a correction.
Steady selling by producers anxious to protect their income in a falling market and persistent rumours that European central banks had sold put the price under pressure.
On Wednesday the Bank of Portugal formally denied it had sold gold from its reserves.
Silver firmed rapidly as gold picked up to be indicated unchanged at $4.81/$4.83 after touching an intraday low of $4.71 when gold was under pressure.
"There was a lot of selling in silver earlier, largely on the back of gold. Now it is doing better than gold," one dealer said.
Platinum and palladium were both relatively quiet.
Platinum was indicated down $0.75 at $372.75/$373.75 and palladium was 50 cents easier at $115.75/$116.75.
